Real `security find-generic-password ... -g` session, captured on real macOS
(Darwin 25.5.0, macOS 26.5.2, 2026-08-14) verifying the fix for the `-w`
hex-corruption bug (docs/notes/test-findings.md #4, MUST_CLEANUP.md 0.7).
Disposable keychain only (`/tmp/mr-secrets-verify/mr-verify.keychain-db`),
never the login keychain; added to the user search list for the session and
removed afterward, keychain file deleted afterward. See
docs/notes/secrets-keychain-notes.md for narrative context and the prior
`-w` session this one follows up on.

Setup:

  security create-keychain -p <throwaway-pw> mr-verify.keychain-db
  security unlock-keychain -p <throwaway-pw> mr-verify.keychain-db
  security list-keychains -d user -s login.keychain-db mr-verify.keychain-db
  security add-generic-password -a "" -s <service> -w "<value>" -A mr-verify.keychain-db
  security find-generic-password -s <service> -g mr-verify.keychain-db

(`-A` — allow any application — used for the same reason the earlier `-w`
session used it: `-T ""` requires an interactive Keychain Access-control
prompt on read-back, which is not what this session was checking.)

Each entry below: stored value, then the exact `password: ...` line `-g`
produced. Every case landed on **stderr**, never stdout, on this machine —
stdout carried only the attribute dump (`keychain:`, `version:`, `class:`,
`attributes:`, one per line) with no `password:` line in it at all. Exit
code was `0` in every successful case.

1. mrv-simple — stored: `sup3rSecret` (plain ASCII, no special characters)
   stderr: password: "sup3rSecret"

2. mrv-multiline — stored: `line1\nline2\nline3` (embedded newlines, no
   trailing one)
   stderr: password: 0x6C696E65310A6C696E65320A6C696E6533  "line1\012line2\012line3"
   Hex decodes to exactly the stored bytes (`6C 69 6E 65 31 0A ...` = `l i n
   e 1 \n ...`). This is the exact case the `BUG:` test in Keychain.test.ts
   pinned against `-w`'s corrupted output.

3. mrv-tab — stored: `tab<TAB>separated` (one embedded tab, 0x09, no
   newlines)
   stderr: password: 0x74616209736570617261746564  "tab\011separated"

4. mrv-pem — stored: a realistic multi-line OpenSSH-private-key-shaped blob
   (280 bytes, no trailing newline of its own)
   stderr: password:   "-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\012b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAAAABG5vbmUAAAAEbm9uZQAAAAAAAAABAAAAMwAAAAtzc2gtZW\012QyNTUxOQAAACD7fakevalueevaluevalueevaluevaluevalueevalueevaluevalueev\012alueevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevalu\012-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"

5. mrv-pem-nl — identical to (4) but with one trailing newline appended to
   the stored value (281 bytes) — the shape a real PEM file on disk usually
   has.
   stderr: password:   "-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\012b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAAAABG5vbmUAAAAEbm9uZQAAAAAAAAABAAAAMwAAAAtzc2gtZW\012QyNTUxOQAAACD7fakevalueevaluevalueevaluevaluevalueevalueevaluevalueev\012alueevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevaluevalu\012-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\012"
   Compared to (4): the hex gained exactly one trailing `0A` and the quoted
   half exactly one trailing `\012`, nothing else — confirming `-g`, unlike
   `-w`, adds no trailing byte of its own; both decoded forms reproduce the
   stored bytes exactly, including a secret whose own final byte is a
   newline.

6. mrv-quote — stored: `say "hi" and \backslash\` (printable ASCII, an
   embedded double quote AND a backslash)
   stderr: password: 0x736179202268692220616E64205C6261636B736C6173685C  "say "hi" and \134backslash\134"
   Note the embedded `"` characters are passed through completely
   unescaped in the quoted half; only the backslash is escaped there (as
   octal `\134`).

7. mrv-backslash — stored: `back\slash` (printable ASCII, one embedded
   backslash, no quote, no non-printable byte)
   stderr: password: 0x6261636B5C736C617368  "back\134slash"
   A literal backslash triggers the `0x` hex fallback on its own, even
   though every byte in the value is printable — the hex fallback is not
   only for non-`isprint()` bytes.

8. mrv-quoteonly — stored: `say "hi" now` (printable ASCII, an embedded
   double quote, no backslash)
   stderr: password: "say "hi" now"
   No `0x` fallback here — a value containing a quote but no backslash and
   no non-printable byte gets *only* the bare quoted form, with the
   embedded quote left raw and unescaped. Still unambiguous to parse
   correctly because the outer quotes are always exactly the line's first
   and last characters, not because of any escaping convention.

9. mrv-apostrophe — stored: `it's fine` (printable ASCII, one embedded
   single quote)
   stderr: password: "it's fine"
   A single quote needs no escaping in this form at all.

10. mrv-utf8 — stored: `café🔑` (UTF-8: `caf` + 0xC3 0xA9 + 0xF0 0x9F 0x94 0x91)
    stderr: password: 0x636166C3A9F09F9491  "caf\303\251\360\237\224\221"
    Confirms the hex fallback also covers multi-byte UTF-8 sequences (each
    non-ASCII byte individually octal-escaped in the quoted half), not just
    the ASCII control characters tested above.

Missing-entry check (unaffected by the `-w` → `-g` switch):

  security find-generic-password -s mrv-does-not-exist -g mr-verify.keychain-db

  exit code: 44
  stderr: security: SecKeychainSearchCopyNext: The specified item could not be found in the keychain.

This is byte-for-byte the same exit code and stderr `-w` produced for a
missing entry (see the doc comment on `isNoSuchKeychainItem` in
`../../src/backends/Keychain.ts`), so `SecretNotFound`'s classification did
not need to change.
